info.title: Queek API Docs
info.description:
Build a store's website on its Queek catalogue: products, collections, promotions, reviews, pages and blog, plus a cart that hands off to Queek checkout. Read llms.txt on this host for the guide.

## Errors

Every error answers `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "errors"?, "doc_url", "request_id"}}`, alongside the
legacy top-level keys. Switch on `error.code`, never on the message. Codes: `ai_unavailable_in_test_mode`, `api_key_expired`, `api_key_mode_mismatch`, `api_key_revoked`, `bad_request`, `client_key_required`, `conflict`, `custom_gateway_forbidden`, `custom_gateway_kyc_required`, `custom_gateway_not_configured`, `custom_gateway_not_verified`, `custom_gateway_plan_required`, `custom_gateway_store_ineligible`, `custom_gateway_verification_failed`, `forbidden`, `gone`, `idempotency_key_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reuse`, `insufficient_scope`, `invalid_client_key`, `metafield_definition_missing`, `metafield_filter_unsupported_type`, `metafield_namespace_reserved`, `metafield_value_invalid`, `metaobject_definition_missing`, `metaobject_field_invalid`, `metaobject_reference_invalid`, `metaobject_type_reserved`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `origin_not_allowed`, `origin_required`, `payload_too_large`, `payment_amount_mismatch`, `plan_inactive`, `route_not_available`, `server_error`, `service_unavailable`, `too_many_requests`, `unauthenticated`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_failed`.
Each error carries `doc_url` pointing at its own entry in the error reference.

## Request ids

Send `X-Request-Id` (8–128 chars matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) to correlate your trace with ours,
or read the one we generate — it is echoed on every response, error bodies included, and appears on every log line
of the request. `X-Queek-Api-Version` carries the API version (`v1`).

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` on a write and a retry cannot execute twice. Same key + same body replays the stored
response verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24h. Same key + a different body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A concurrent duplicate waits 15s for the first to finish, then replays;
past that it is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Responses ≥ 400 are not stored, so a failure stays retryable.
The slot is vendor + caller + METHOD:path + key. The body is the fingerprint, not part of the slot. Operations that accept the header document it as a parameter.

## Rate limits

180 requests/min per API key + IP, or storefront origin + IP when no key is sent. On top of that, a private (`sk_live_`) key carries its
store's plan quota: `free` 60/min, `social_media` 120/min, `starter` 120/min, `growth` 240/min, `scale` 1200/min, `enterprise` 2400/min. sk_live_ private keys only. A pk_live_ public key is shared by every visitor of the store, so it gets no per-store bucket.
Exceeding either is `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an endpoint per store and Queek posts the signed event to it. Topics are listed under `webhooks`
in this document; the body is signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>` —
over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, tolerance 300s. A rotation keeps the previous secret valid for
24h and sends both signatures, space delimited. Delivery is 8 attempts on a published backoff;
an endpoint failing for 24h is disabled and the merchant notified.

get.description:
A developer (or a theme, or an AI builder) reading `metafields` off a
product has no way to know what `custom.fabric` means, what type it is or
what values are allowed unless the schema is readable too. Values are
already public on the product; this exposes only their shape, never a
value, and never a definition belonging to another store.

Scoped to `client_schema_owner_types`, NOT every owner type: order
definitions are a description of a merchant's back office and no order
metafield value is ever public, so their schema stays on the vendor API.
get.summary: The store's metafield SCHEMA on the public Storefront API

get.description: The store's published catalogue, paginated (`page`, `per_page` ≤ 100). Filter with `keyword`, `category_slug` (or `category_id`), `sort` (`latest|popular|price_low|price_high`), `has_video`, and `metafield[namespace.key]=value` (typed, exact match against the store's own definitions — see `GET /store/metafield-definitions`; an undefined handle answers 422 `metafield_definition_missing`). Walk `pagination.current_page` … `pagination.last_page` to read everything. Every `price` is the final customer price.

parameters.name: metafield
parameters.description: Filter by a defined metafield: `metafield[custom.fabric]=cotton`. Up to 5 handles, ANDed. Values are compared using the definition's type (integer 10 matches 10, not 100). Undefined handle → 422 `metafield_definition_missing`.

parameters.name: X-Client-Key
parameters.description: Your store API key (Dashboard → Settings → API keys). `pk_live_…` public keys are for browser code and only work from an origin on the key's allowlist; `sk_live_…` private keys are for servers and native apps and need no Origin.

metafields.description:
The receiver's own fields coming back to them: typed metafields the
merchant defined, and the opaque metadata an integrator wrote. This
is the whole point of order extensions — a webhook that omits the
ERP id forces the receiver to make a second call to match the order
to their own record.

QueekError.description: The one error shape every Queek API surface answers with.

code.description: Stable identifier a client switches on. A new failure mode gets a new code; an existing code never changes meaning.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable — never switch on it.

field.description: First offending field, on validation failures only.

errors.description: Per-field validation messages, on validation failures only.

doc_url.description: Deep link to this code in the error reference: https://docs.usequeek.com/docs/versioning-and-errors#<code>.

request_id.description: The X-Request-Id of this request. Quote it in support.

status.description: Legacy top-level key, kept for clients that predate the envelope.

QueekError.title: QueekError

QueekMetafieldType.description:
A metafield definition's `type`. Scalar forms, plus `list.<type>` for each listable one.

Limits (shared Postgres, part of the contract): 200 definitions per store, 50 values per resource, 65536 bytes per serialized value. Free-form `metadata`: 50 keys, key ≤ 64 chars, value ≤ 500 chars.

Reserved namespaces (a store may not define in these): `queek`.
Owner types wired in this version: `product`, `order`.
QueekMetafieldType.title: QueekMetafieldType

QueekWebhookEvent.description: The signed body of a webhook delivery. Signed as `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}` with HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>`; verify before trusting it.

id.description: Event id, identical to the `webhook-id` header. Dedupe on it — a retry reuses it.

api_version.description: Payload contract version. Additive within a major.

QueekWebhookEvent.title: QueekWebhookEvent

QueekWebhookTopic.description:
`orders/create` — An order was placed, on any channel.
`orders/paid` — An order moved to paid.
`orders/updated` — An order changed — status, fulfilment stage or any merchant action.
`orders/fulfilled` — An order was completed or delivered.
`orders/cancelled` — An order was cancelled or rejected.
QueekWebhookTopic.title: QueekWebhookTopic

partial.description:
Opt-in only — omitted/false keeps store() byte-identical to before,
which matters because /v1/carts (mobile) maps to this same method.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.

post.description:
An order was placed, on any channel.

Delivered to every active endpoint of the store subscribed to this topic. Verify the signature, dedupe on the event `id`, acknowledge with a 2xx inside 5s, and do the work asynchronously.

200.description: Acknowledged. Any other status (or a timeout) is retried on the published backoff schedule.
